messages:
maria: Heads-up — DSAR lodged for user acct 892, requests full erasure of profile + conversation embeddings. Root ticket #PRIV-2026-81
sam: On it. Quick scan: embeddings stored in vector-store (eu-prod), backups in gcs snapshots, and nightly ES snapshots. KMS key id: projects/redwood-keystore/keys/eu-vec-key
chris: Legal confirms verified requester. They explicitly requested complete deletion (right to be forgotten). Need audit trail for every deletion step.
maria: Blocking issue: svc-dsar-runner lacks keystore.decrypt on eu-keystore. Current rolebinding only covers read. If we grant keystore.delete across tenants we risk cross-account escalation.
sam: Proposed short-term: create rolebinding "keystore-dsar-runner" limited to eu-prod namespace + scope only to key eu-vec-key. No wildcard. Then run deletion job.
jess: Product: user said delete, not pseudonymize. Also flag: embeddings might be referenced by indexes in other customers? We must ensure idempotent deletion and orphan removal.
maria: Also found an audit gap: delete events from 2025-11-02 03:20 -> 03:40 are missing for vector-service. Looks like the audit agent restarted during key rotation.
ops-bot: note: automated alert — keystore rotation completed 2025-11-02T03:18Z; rotation job suppresses key material logs per design. :warning:
sam: That explains suppressed key id in logs. For DSAR we need supplemental evidence: KMS rotation manifest + vm serial logs + db delete query logs.
chris: Legal: acceptable if we can show correlated artifacts and a signed deletion manifest. Also preserve chain-of-custody for 90 days.
maria: Do we need a temporary retention exception for backups? GCS snapshots contain clear copies. If we delete from live store, backups still have data.
sam: Two options — (1) run targeted snapshot rewrite to scrub user rows and re-snapshot (manual, slow) or (2) request retention-exception + schedule secure deletion of affected snapshots within 30 days.
jess: Product prefers option 2 if legal permits because 1 will be expensive and risk-wide IO.
chris: Legal accepts retention-exception route if we: a) record exception request, b) redact metadata references, c) commit target deletion date, d) provide signed affidavit.
maria: Ok. Action plan:
- sam: create rolebinding 'keystore-dsar-runner' scoped to eu-vec-key by EOD today (3361242000)
- sam: run deletion job against vector-store and DB (runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dsar-delete)
- ops: dump KMS rotation manifest + vm serial logs and attach to PRIV-2026-81
- chris: prepare signed deletion affidavit and retention-exception form
- jess: notify customer with expected timeline (30 days)
sam: One more: add an audit log patch to ensure delete actions include key_id in future (tracking: ENG-5142)
maria: I'll own postmortem for the audit gap. Schedule internal review.
chris: Thanks all. @sam @maria mark when the rolebinding is applied and job started. :thumbsup:
sam: rolebinding created in eu-prod (just now). starting deletion job, will post progress.
maria: deletion job finished — verified 6 records removed, vector-index shards updated. attaching log snippet:
```
> DELETE FROM user_profiles WHERE user_id = 892;
rows_affected=6
vector-store: delete success shard-3,shard-7
```
chris: Received logs and affidavit draft. Legal signs off on retention exception and timeline.
jess: Customer notified, they acknowledged. Closing loop in PRIV-2026-81.
ops-bot: alert cleared — snapshot-deletion-schedule set for 2025-12-01T05:00Z.
